text:
[verdict]
In the 50 retrieved episodes where the tape looked like this, SPY and its analogs produced a median 5-session return of -0.1%, with outcomes ranging from -5.12% to 6.88%. The single number to anchor on is that 52% of those historical paths finished below zero, while the 10th percentile loss was -2.39%. This describes a conditional distribution that is roughly symmetric but slightly skewed toward modest losses, not a forecast of what will happen next.

[state]
The engine pulled these 50 analogs—spanning 28 distinct sessions and 22 symbols between 2016-12-14 and 2026-09-08—because the current state is defined by three distinctive features. First, the 20-session dollar-volume regime z-score (dv20z) sits at -1.985, meaning liquidity is unusually thin. Second, WTI crude change over 20 days (oilChg20) is up 19.24%, a sharp energy shock. Third, 20-session realised volatility (vol20) is compressed at 9.16%. These features carry heavy weight in the retrieval metric: dv20z, oilChg20, and vol20 are part of the name and macro groups, which together account for 50% of the distance calculation. The combination of low volume, an oil spike, and quiet volatility pulls recent broad-market ETFs into the neighborhood, alongside older matches like SPY on 2016-12-14.

[history]
Over the 5-session horizon, the mean return across the 50 analogs was -0.03% and the median was -0.1%, with a standard deviation of 2.14%. The distribution has a slight positive skew of 0.51. The 25th percentile was -1.31% and the 75th percentile was 0.92%. At the extremes, the worst outcome was -5.12% and the best was 6.88%. In 48% of the cases the path finished above zero, and in 52% it finished below. Only 2% of the analogs fell below -5%, and none breached -10%. The bad tail is populated by very recent history: IWM on 2026-09-08 returned -2.98%, SPY on 2026-09-03 returned -1.15%, JPM on 2026-09-04 returned -2.37%, and DIA on 2026-09-02 returned -1.86%. Conversely, the upside tail includes SPY on 2025-06-20 returning 3.47% and BAC on 2026-08-31 returning 1.24%. The closest match overall was IWM on 2026-09-08 at a distance of 0.2997.

[tails]
A position can end near flat and still be un-holdable through the week. Across the 50 analogs, the median maximum adverse excursion—the worst intra-horizon drawdown before the 5-session close—was -1.05%. The 25th percentile of max adverse excursion was -1.98%, and the 10th percentile was -3.1%. On the upside, the median max favourable excursion was 0.99%, with the 75th percentile at 1.89% and the 90th percentile at 3.52%. The reward-to-risk ratio based on these excursions is 0.94. Looking at specific drawdown breaches, only 4% of the analog paths experienced a 5% drawdown at any point during the 5 sessions. None of the retrieved episodes breached a 10%, 15%, or 20% drawdown threshold.

[stress]
When conditioned on historical stress regimes, the baseline picture changes materially in some scenarios and barely moves in others. The 2020-02/03 liquidity crash scenario is the most severe: across 48 analogs, the median forward return was -4.61%, which is -4.51% worse than the baseline. The 10th percentile plunged to -11.63%, and 41.7% of paths breached a 10% drawdown. However, central-bank backstops arrived inside that window, so the realised rebound is baked into the forward returns; it is a sample of one regime, not a forecast of the next one. The 2025-04 tariff shock used 26 analogs and produced a median of -0.92% (-0.82% vs baseline), but its 10th percentile reached -11.26%, with 23.1% of paths breaching a 10% drawdown. Policy reversals inside that window make the tail asymmetric in a way specific to that episode. The 2022 inflation/rate bear yielded a median of -2.09% (-1.99% vs baseline) and a 10th percentile of -5.01%, with 2% breaching a 10% drawdown. Because it is a nine-month window sampled repeatedly under a per-date cap of 2 analogs, treat it as a regime description, not 50 independent events. The 2018-Q4 tightening scare produced a median of -1.09% (-0.99% vs baseline) and a 10th percentile of -4.75%, with 0% breaching a 10% drawdown. It ended with a policy pivot in January 2019, which flatters the forward returns of late-window analogs. The 2024-08-05 carry unwind had a median of -0.49% (-0.39% vs baseline) and a 10th percentile of -4.04%, with 2.8% breaching a 10% drawdown. The reversal was almost as fast as the drawdown, so H-day forward returns look benign even though the intra-horizon excursion did not. The 2023-03 regional bank stress actually improved the median to 1.41% (+1.51% vs baseline) with a 10th percentile of -1.59% and 0% breaching a 10% drawdown. The window is very short, so the analog set is dominated by a handful of sessions. Among the shock scenarios, earnings release day shifted the median to -0.79% (-0.69% vs baseline) with a 10th percentile of -6.71% and 2% breaching a 10% drawdown. Earnings dates for foreign private issuers come from 6-K full-text search and are noisier than 8-K Item 2.02 dates. Volatility spike (+2 sigma VIX) produced a median of -0.2% (-0.1% vs baseline) and a 10th percentile of -4.18%, with 4% breaching a 10% drawdown. VIX shocks mean-revert quickly, stressing entry timing more than terminal value. Liquidity air pocket gave a median of -0.13% (-0.03% vs baseline) and a 10th percentile of -4.2%, with 4% breaching a 10% drawdown. The gap20 feature is measured on the underlying exchange session, not a 7x24 venue, bounding reference-market gap risk only. Crypto contagion, China ADR de-rating, FOMC decision day, and policy-rate path re-pricing all produced medians within roughly 0.2% of the baseline and 0% probability of breaching a 10% drawdown. For crypto contagion, the BTC feature is a market-wide proxy and name-level linkage is unidentified. For China ADR, delisting risks are structural and absent from the price/vol feature space. For FOMC, only 92 decision days exist, making the analog set small and overlapping. For rate re-pricing, DGS3MO/T10Y2Y levels are proxies, and transmission depends on duration not captured here. No scenarios were skipped by the engine.

[limits]
This analysis has concrete limits. The engine's own validation states: "Analog retrieval hits its coverage target out of sample and its width tracks each instrument's own volatility, but it is NOT sharper than a same-name unconditional band at matched coverage, and its raw PIT distribution fails a uniformity test. It is a stress-testing and provenance instrument, not an alpha source." Specifically, the conformal interval achieves 80.8% out-of-sample coverage with a width of 10.4%, but the matched-coverage sharpness versus the same-name unconditional benchmark is -7.6%, meaning the naive benchmark is tighter. The directional hit rate is 50.1%, and the PIT chi-square statistic is 208.6 against a 5% critical value of 16.92, confirming the probability integral transform fails uniformity. The dataset spans 2513 sessions and 71 symbols from 2016-09-20 to 2026-09-18. Prices are sourced keyless from api.stockanalysis.com, and earnings dates rely on SEC full-text search clustered at 6 calendar days. If you trade this via the tokenised wrapper SPYG_USDT on Gate.io spot v4, its status is measured. The reference cash market is shut for 81.4% of the week, and 60.97% of the wrapper's own realised hourly movement happened in those closed hours. It is classified as a fair tracker with a return correlation of 0.9358 and a tracking error of 25 bp/day. The premium band over the raw close is -0.08% to 0.31%, and the spread is 16.66 bps. As the card notes, a fair tracker is not the underlying—at 25 bp/day of tracking error the wrapper carries idiosyncratic risk, and the premium band means your exit price can differ from the reference close the analog distribution is built on. These wrapper figures were measured on Gate.io, not Bitget, and nothing here feeds the retrieval engine or the conformal scale.
